outcomes: Apply course concepts, theories and research findings to the student’s own lifespan development and to real-world problems
Describe, explain, evaluate and apply concepts in developmental psychology and convey these appraisals effectively through multiple communication modalities (writing, oral and interpersonal)
Describe, distinguish and evaluate major theoretical perspectives and issues and the findings from major psychological studies in developmental psychology
objectives: Define and provide examples of the major developmental issues of nature vs. nurture, continuity vs. discontinuity; stability vs. change, universality vs. context-specificity

Describe, compare and contrast the major theoretical viewpoints in human development, including, but not limited to: biological, psychodynamic, learning, humanistic, cognitive-developmental, social-cognitive and systems theories (including how different theoretical perspectives affect or determine the research and applications that arise from them).

Describe the techniques and research methods used by developmental psychologists to study lifespan development and analyze elements of a scientific approach to understanding human development in a biopsychosocial context.

Describe and critically evaluate theories and research relevant to development in areas which may include (but are not limited to) physical development, sensory and perceptual development, motor development, cognitive development, language development, social development, emotional development, personality development, gender identity and sexual development, moral development, disturbances in development and psychopathology, death/dying.

Describe the developing person at the following life stages from conception to death: prenatal, infancy, early childhood, middle and late childhood, adolescence, early adulthood, middle adulthood, late adulthood, and death/dying, and discuss the effects of earlier life stage experiences on later behavior and development.
Identify biological, psychological, and sociocultural influences on lifespan development.
Describe the ways in which psychological principles and research apply to real world problems and issues across the lifespan.
Identify possible causes or sources of developmental change and reasons for disturbances in the developmental process.

rows.title: Troubleshooting & Repair of HIGH-VOLTAGE SYSTEMS
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
outcomes: Work safely on high voltage vehicle systems;
Employ correct PPE while working with high voltage vehicle systems;
Understand and analyze high voltage vehicle safety systems.
objectives: Apply principles of shop safety in accordance with CAL/OSHA;
Test, evaluate the condition of high voltage gloves and PPE;
Demonstrate the general sequential steps in performing the disabling of a high voltage circuit;
Create approach boundary areas for vehicles with exposed moveable conductor and exposed fixed circuit;
Identify high voltage components by visual identification;
Locate high voltage components on the vehicle using service information;
Properly select and use testing tools/equipment to measure high voltage circuits;
Select tools, associated accessories, approved by industry standards;
Appraise the condition and clean a High Voltage Manual Service Disconnect;
Identify Interlock Circuits with electrical diagrams;
Test functionality of Interlock Circuits using hand-held meters, scan tools;
Perform active high voltage bus discharge circuit test using a hand-held meter, scan tool, and service information;
Perform a passive high voltage bus discharge circuit test using a hand-held meter, scan tool, and service information;
Evaluate functionality of a high voltage isolation fault detection circuit by using Off-Board electrical tools, hand-held meter, scan tool, and service information;
Determine location of an insulation resistance failure, using vehicle on-board diagnostics systems;
Perform insulation resistance testing on high voltage components by using insulation meter and service information;
Perform calculations that determine the minimal threshold level for an isolation, fault detection diagnostic systems.
